questions.q: What message was revealed to Daniel in the third year of Cyrus king of Persia?
questions.a: The message was about a great war.

questions.q: How was Daniel able to understand the message?
questions.a: Daniel understood the message because he had insight from a vision.

questions.q: How long was Daniel mourning?
questions.a: Daniel was mourning for three weeks.

questions.q: What did Daniel not do during those three weeks?
questions.a: He did not eat any fine food or meat, drink wine, or put oil on himself.

questions.q: Where was Daniel on the twenty-fourth day of the first month?
questions.a: He was beside the great river, the Tigris.

questions.q: Who did Daniel see in his vision?
questions.a: He saw a man dressed in linen with a fine gold belt around his waist.

questions.q: What was the man in Daniel’s vision like?
questions.a: The man’s body was like beryl, his face was like lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and feet were like polished bronze, and the sound of his words was like the sound of a multitude.

questions.q: What happened to the men who were with Daniel?
questions.a: They did not see the vision, but they were terrified and ran away to hide themselves.

questions.q: What was Daniel’s response when he saw the great vision and heard the man’s words?
questions.a: Daniel’s face turned pale, and no strength remained in him. He fell into a deep sleep with his face to the ground.

questions.q: What happened when the hand touched Daniel?
questions.a: It made him get up, trembling, onto his hands and knees.

questions.q: What did the man tell Daniel to do?
questions.a: He told Daniel to understand the words he was about to speak and to stand up, because he had been sent to him.

questions.q: When was the angel sent to Daniel?
questions.a: The angel was sent on the first day Daniel set his mind to understand and humble himself before God.

questions.q: Why did it take the angel twenty-one days to come to Daniel?
questions.a: The angel was detained by the prince of the kingdom of Persia who resisted him.

questions.q: When will the events of the vision happen?
questions.a: The vision was about the last days, the days yet to come.

questions.q: What did Daniel do while the man was speaking to him?
questions.a: Daniel looked down at the ground and said nothing.

questions.q: What did Daniel say the vision had done to him?
questions.a: Daniel said the vision had greatly upset him, and that he had no strength left and could hardly breathe.

questions.q: What did the one with an appearance like a human being do to strengthen Daniel?
questions.a: The one who looked like a human being touched Daniel to strengthen him.

questions.q: What did the man tell Daniel?
questions.a: He told Daniel not to be afraid, wished him peace, and told him to be strong.

questions.q: What did the one who looked like a human being say he was going to do after he left Daniel?
questions.a: He said he was returning to fight against the prince of Persia.

questions.q: What did the one who looked like a human being say he was going to tell Daniel?
questions.a: He said he was going to tell Daniel what was written in the book of truth.

commentary.text: Daniel's vision near the river Hiddekel. (Dan. 10:1-9) He is to expect a discovery of future events. (Dan. 10:10-21)

Dan. 10:1-9. This chapter relates the beginning of Daniel's last vision, which is continued to the end of the book. The time would be long before all would be accomplished; and much of it is not yet fulfilled. Christ appeared to Daniel in a glorious form, and it should engage us to think highly and honourably of him. Let us admire his condescension for us and our salvation. There remained no strength in Daniel. The greatest and best of men cannot bear the full discoveries of the Divine glory; for no man can see it, and live; but glorified saints see Christ as he is, and can bear the sight. How dreadful soever Christ may appear to those under convictions of sin, there is enough in his word to quiet their spirits.

Dan. 10:10-21 Whenever we enter into communion with God, it becomes us to have a due sense of the infinite distance between us and the holy God. How shall we, that are dust and ashes, speak to the Lord of glory? Nothing is more likely, nothing more effectual to revive the drooping spirits of the saints, than to be assured of God's love to them. From the very first day we begin to look toward God in a way of duty, he is ready to meet us in the way of mercy. Thus ready is God to hear prayer. When the angel had told the prophet of the things to come, he was to return, and oppose the decrees of the Persian kings against the Jews. The angels are employed as God's ministering servants, Heb. 1:14. Though much was done against the Jews by the kings of Persia, God permitting it, much more mischief would have been done if God had not prevented it. He would now more fully show what were God's purposes, of which the prophecies form an outline; and we are concerned to study what is written in these Scriptures of truth, for they belong to our everlasting peace. While Satan and his angels, and evil counsellors, excite princes to mischief against the church, we may rejoice that Christ our Prince, and all his mighty angels, act against our enemies; but we ought not to expect many to favour us in this evil world. Yet the whole counsel of God shall be established; and let each one pray, Lord Jesus, be our righteousness now, and thou wilt be our everlasting confidence, through life, in death, at the day of judgment, and for evermore.
